TensorFold's GLM engine hardcodes cuda:0; the container entrypoint patches it to honor TF_GLM_DEVICE per rank.

## Executive Summary

This report analyzes 18 equipment records spanning five asset classes (turbines, compressors, condensers, valves, pumps, heat exchangers, and pipelines) across stations ranging from 15 to 353. The analysis identifies several units warranting immediate attention — most notably **pump 5993 (vibration 7.8 mm/s)**, **compressor 2524 (vibration 8.7 mm/s)**, and **pump 7776 (vibration 5.9 mm/s)** — and flags thermodynamic anomalies such as the **heat exchanger 4564 operating at −16 °C**, which suggests either a sensor fault, loss of heat input, or unintended cooling. The report is organized into: (1) methodology and reference thresholds, (2) unit-by-unit analysis, (3) cross-fleet pattern analysis, (4) prioritized maintenance actions, and (5) recommendations for instrumentation and data-quality improvements.

# Technical Analysis of Plant Condition-Monitoring Records (Records 0000000–0000017)

## 1. Scope and Method

This report analyzes 18 condition-monitoring records spanning six asset classes (condensers, reactors, scrubbers, valves, compressors, heat exchangers, pipelines, and turbines) across 17 stations. Each record contains five measurement channels: pressure (kPa), temperature (°C), flow (m³/h), vibration velocity RMS (mm/s), and thermal/operating efficiency (%).

The analysis proceeds in three stages:

1. **Population-level screening** — establishing the statistical envelope of the fleet so that individual anomalies are judged against peer behavior rather than absolute thresholds alone.
2. **Asset-by-asset assessment** — identifying likely failure modes for each unit, ranked by severity.
3. **Maintenance action plan** — concrete, prioritized interventions with recommended follow-up measurements.

Because the dataset is small (n = 18), statistical conclusions are indicative rather than definitive. Where a single reading is the sole evidence, I flag the confidence level accordingly and recommend confirming measurements before intrusive work.

# Technical Analysis of Plant Condition Monitoring Records

## 1. Scope and Method

This report analyzes 18 condition-monitoring records (Records 0000000–0000017) covering eight asset classes — condenser, turbine, scrubber, valve, pump, separator, pipeline, compressor, reactor, and heat exchanger — across 17 stations. Each record contains five measured parameters: pressure (kPa), temperature (°C), flow (m³/h), vibration velocity (mm/s RMS), and efficiency (%).

The analysis proceeds in three stages:

1. **Screening** of each record against typical alarm thresholds for its asset class.
2. **Failure-mode inference** — identifying the most probable degradation mechanisms consistent with the measured signature.
3. **Prioritized maintenance actions**, with recommended follow-up measurements.

Because the records are single snapshots (no trend history), conclusions are probabilistic. Where a measurement is ambiguous, I state the alternative interpretations and the additional data needed to discriminate between them. The most diagnostic single parameter in this dataset is **vibration velocity**, and the second most diagnostic is the **flow/pressure relationship**; efficiency is a useful corroborating indicator but is slow-moving and rarely points to a single root cause.

# Technical Analysis of Plant Equipment Records — Stations 13–381

## 1. Scope and Method

This report analyzes 18 equipment records spanning six asset classes (pumps, scrubbers, heat exchangers, reactors, condensers, compressors, separators, turbines) across 18 stations. Each record contains five process/condition parameters: discharge pressure, process temperature, flow rate, casing vibration velocity (RMS, mm/s), and thermal/overall efficiency.

## 1. Scope and Data Overview

This report analyzes 18 condition-monitoring records spanning six asset classes (condensers, scrubbers, heat exchangers, compressors, pipelines, separators, reactors, and pumps) across 17 stations. Each record contains five measurement channels: pressure (kPa), temperature (°C), flow (m³/h), vibration velocity (mm/s RMS), and thermal/operating efficiency (%).

- **Record 0000004 (heat exchanger 1128)** reports a temperature of 0 °C and **Record 0000016 (condenser 4963)** reports −4 °C. # Technical Analysis of Plant Equipment Records: Stations 61–397

## Executive Summary

This report analyzes 18 equipment records spanning six asset classes (separators, pumps, scrubbers, valves, compressors, pipelines, turbines, heat exchangers, and one reactor) across stations 61 through 397. The analysis identifies **five units requiring immediate intervention**, **four units warranting enhanced monitoring**, and **nine units operating within expected parameters**. The dominant failure signatures are elevated vibration on rotating equipment (compressors, pumps, pipelines), anomalous flow conditions suggesting blockage or valve malfunction, and thermal excursions on separation and heat-transfer equipment.
